record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Determine whether there exists a real Banach space X other than the scalar field ℝ itself such that n^(2)(X) = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 44. Is there any real Banach space X different from R such that n(2)(X) = 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space over the real field, and let L(X) denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on X with the operator norm. For T ∈ L(X), the numerical radius of T is defined by
  v(T) = sup{ |x*(T x)| : x ∈ X, x* ∈ X*, ‖x‖ = ‖x*‖ = x*(x) = 1 }.
The skew-Hermitian part (Lie algebra) of L(X) is
  Z(X) = { T ∈ L(X) : v(T) = 0 },
and on the quotient space L(X)/Z(X) one considers the quotient norm ‖[T]‖ = inf{ ‖T + S‖ : S ∈ Z(X) }. The second numerical index of X is defined as
  n^{(2)}(X) = inf{ v(T) : T ∈ L(X), ‖[T]‖ = 1 },
equivalently, the largest constant k ≥ 0 such that k · ‖[T]‖ ≤ v(T) for every T ∈ L(X). One always has 0 ≤ n^{(2)}(X) ≤ 1, and for the one-dimensional space ℝ one trivially has n^{(2)}(ℝ) = 1.

Question: Does there exist a real Banach space X, with X ≠ ℝ (i.e. of dimension at least 2), such that n^{(2)}(X) = 1?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the affirmative. A subsequent work introducing and studying the second numerical index proves that every real Hilbert space has second numerical index equal to 1, providing a family of real Banach spaces other than ℝ with n^{(2)}(X) = 1.

status_evidence.title: On a second numerical index for Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: we prove that Hilbert spaces have second numerical index one and that they are the only spaces with this property among the class of Banach spaces with one-unconditional basis and non-trivial Lie algebra.
status_evidence.claim: Real Hilbert spaces have second numerical index equal to 1, so spaces X ≠ ℝ with n^{(2)}(X)=1 exist.

status_evidence.title: On a second numerical index for Banach spaces (Proc. Royal Soc. Edinburgh A)
status_evidence.snippet: Hilbert spaces have second numerical index one ... finite-dimensional Banach spaces have positive second numerical index.
status_evidence.claim: Published result establishing n^{(2)}(H)=1 for Hilbert spaces.
